## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The official Kāngxī-court daily-lecture (*rì jiǎng* 日講) commentary on the *Shàngshū* 尚書 ([KR1b0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0001)) in 13 *juǎn*, compiled between Kāngxī 17 / 1678 and Kāngxī 19 / 1680 by an imperial commission under Kuldena 庫勒納 and [葉方藹](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%91%89%E6%96%B9%E8%97%B9) (Yè Fāngǎi, 1629–1682). The work was prepared for the Kāngxī emperor's personal *jīng yán* 經筵 study sessions, then printed with an imperial preface (Kāngxī 19 / 1680.IV.12) and promulgated to officials throughout the empire as the authoritative Kāngxī-era *Shū* commentary. It is the institutional precursor to the much larger *Yùdìng Shū jīng zhuàn shuō huì zuǎn* 御定書經傳說彙纂 (later Kāngxī era), which became the *Yùdìng* imperial standard for the Yōngzhèng-Qiánlóng *Shū* curriculum.

The Kāngxī emperor's preface lays out the work's doctrinal program with unusual clarity: the *Shàngshū* records the *zhì fǎ* 治法 ("methods of government") of the four dynasties (Yú-Xià-Shāng-Zhōu), but these are grounded in *xīn fǎ* 心法 ("methods of the heart-mind") whose three core virtues are *jìng* 敬 (reverence), *chéng* 誠 (sincerity), and *zhōng* 中 (the mean). The preface catalogs canonical phrases under each of these three headings (*qīn míng* 欽明, *yín gōng* 寅恭, *zhī jù* 祗懼, *dí wèi* 迪畏 are *jìng*-class; *yǔn sài* 允塞, *zhì xián* 至諴, *yī dé* 一德, *dūn xìn* 惇信 are *chéng*-class; *yì zhì shì lǐ zhì xīn* 義制事禮制心, *chén qián gāng kè gāo míng róu kè* 沈潛剛克高明柔克, *kuān ér yǒu zhì cōngróng yǐ hé* 寬而有制從容以和 are *zhōng*-class), and classifies the canonical sage-kings by their relation to the *xīn fǎ*: Yáo, Shùn, Yǔ, and Wén are "*xìng zhī*" (innate); Tāng, Wǔ, Gāozōng are "*shēn zhī*" (embodied); Tài Jiǎ and Chéng Wáng are "*kùn ér xué zhī*" (forced and learned); Tài Kāng, Jié, and Zhòu are "*bèi ér qù zhī*" (deviated and abandoned). This four-fold classification is one of the cleaner late-Imperial statements of the post-Cài Shěn *xīnfǎ* doctrine of *Shàngshū* canonical-political theology.

**Abstract**

The *Rì jiǎng Shū jīng jiě yì* is the institutional Kāngxī-court statement of *Shàngshū* doctrine, prepared as the imperial daily-lecture text and promulgated through the empire as the standard. Its institutional position is significant: in the post-1313 *Càizhuàn* curricular tradition, the imperial center had progressively substituted its own commentaries for Cài Shěn's, with the Hóngwǔ *Huì xuǎn* ([KR1b0036](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0036), 1394) taking the first step (correcting Cài on 66 specific points), the Yǒnglè *Dàquán* ([KR1b0037](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1b/KR1b0037), 1415) re-canonizing Cài, and now the Kāngxī *Rì jiǎng* (1680) and the later *Yùdìng Huì zuǎn* re-establishing imperial-court arbitration over Cài via the synthesizing daily-lecture format.

The composition window is fixed (1678–1680): formal commission Kāngxī 17 / 1678.II.2; completion and imperial preface Kāngxī 19 / 1680.IV.12. The submission to the *Sìkù* was Qiánlóng 40 / 1775, in the early wave of *Sìkù* *Shū lèi* entries.

The doctrinal program — set out in the imperial preface — is the *xīnfǎ* 心法 / *zhìfǎ* 治法 distinction, with the three core virtues (*jìng*, *chéng*, *zhōng*) anchoring the *xīnfǎ*. This is essentially the Cài Shěn / Zhū Xī orthodox reading of the *Shàngshū* — the *Dà Yǔ mó* sixteen-character formula (*rén xīn wéi wēi, dào xīn wéi wéi, wéi jīng wéi yī, yǔn zhí jué zhōng*) is the unstated foundation — but the imperial preface is unusually explicit in cataloging which canonical phrases belong to which doctrinal category. The four-fold classification of sage-kings (innate / embodied / forced / deviated) gives the doctrine a graduated psychological-political application that the Sòng-Yuán-Míng Càizhuàn tradition had largely left implicit.

The *Sìkù tíyào* is unusually deferential — emphasizing the Kāngxī emperor's personal contribution and casting the human compilers' role as merely supportive. This is the standard reverential mode for imperial-commission entries; the *tíyào* does not engage the work's substantive readings (as it would for a private commentary) but only the institutional fact of its production. The closing formula — "*jūn shī tǒng yī*" 君師統一 ("the sovereign and the teacher are one") — is the classical-political topos asserting that the emperor as classical lecturer-on-his-own-canon-curriculum embodies both political and pedagogical authority.

The work served as the immediate model for the parallel *Rì jiǎng Sì shū jiě yì* 日講四書解義 (already published in 1677, before the *Shū* project's commission), the *Rì jiǎng Yìjīng jiě yì* 日講易經解義 (Kāngxī 22 / 1683), and other Kāngxī-era imperial daily-lecture commentaries on the canon. As a group these works represent the Kāngxī court's institutional re-claiming of canonical-curricular authority from the late-Míng commercial cram-book industry that had developed around the post-Yǒnglè *Dàquán* Càizhuàn monopoly.
